name: Self-running generative ambient soundscape built from per-layer clip pools that pick their next clip by weighted chance (about 50/50 repeat vs jump, with silent and sparse clips to weight density), over a reverbed noise/field-recording foundation, a tonic drone and a root bass note at random intervals, with sample-and-hold auto-pan on random one-shot FX and weighted-probability quantized note sequences
goal: Build an ambient soundscape that keeps evolving on its own so you can focus on sound design and later harvest the best stretches. Layers: (1) a sonic foundation of field recording or noise run through a lot of reverb, plus a granular noise layer whose playheads are modulated; (2) a drone pad on the tonic chord (E minor in the video) with several slow modulators on its macros; (3) a simple FM bass with a little chorus that plays the root at random intervals. Give every track a pool of pre-built clips (including pure-silence clips and busier vs sparser variants) and a follow action on every clip: when a clip ends it either repeats or jumps to another clip, with a probability slider (about 50/50 in the video). Add a random one-shot layer: a single MIDI note through a random-pitch MIDI effect into a drum-rack/sampler of chosen FX one-shots, ending in an auto-pan driven by a sample-and-hold LFO. Use per-note chance and a velocity range on clips, and inside the synth use three independent sample-and-hold modulators on different parameters, a repeating (Turing-machine-style) random sequence quantized to the minor scale, and a step sequencer with weighted note probabilities (root high, others medium or low).

prerequisites: A DAW with clip launching and follow actions (or a scheduler that can pick the next clip by weighted chance)
A synth with sample-and-hold/random modulators, pitch quantize and a step sequencer (or equivalent MIDI tools)
A small set of field recordings / noise sources and FX one-shots you are allowed to use

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Tonic minor key, e.g. E minor

inputs.name: clip_pools
inputs.description: Per track: list of clips, including at least one silence clip and sparse/busy variants

inputs.name: repeat_probability
inputs.description: Chance a clip repeats instead of jumping (about 0.5 in the video)

outputs.name: harvest
outputs.description: Recorded long run to cut favourite passages from

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.

Vendor tools in the video (DAW follow actions, synth random/sequencer pages) are mapped to generic clip-scheduler, random MIDI, sample-and-hold and quantizer modules; no presets or factory noise samples are copied.

Matt prefers steady melodies: use a repeating (locked) random sequence or weighted step probabilities with the root high, never free-running random pitch wobble; keep randomness on clip choice, panning, velocity and timbre.
If the piece has drums or a pulse, keep that layer's pool free of long silence clips at the start so the beat arrives early (about 8 bars).
Polyrhythm Studio mapping: each layer = a clip pool with a weighted next-clip state machine evaluated at clip end.

steps.action: Create the foundation: a field-recording or noise track through a lot of reverb, plus a granular noise layer with its playheads/position modulated.
Add a drone pad on the tonic chord and route several slow modulators (LFOs, random) to its macros.
steps.expect: A tonal centre that never sits still.

steps.action: Add a simple FM bass with a little chorus that plays the root note at random intervals.
steps.expect: Occasional low anchors on the tonic.

steps.action: For each track, build a pool of clips: varied patterns, sparser and busier ones, and at least one clip of pure silence.
steps.expect: Each layer has several options of different density.

steps.action: Turn on a follow action for every clip: after it finishes, repeat itself or jump to another clip in the pool; set the probability slider (about 50/50 to start) and weight it by clip content.
steps.expect: Every layer wanders between its clips and sometimes falls silent.

steps.action: Random one-shots: feed one MIDI note through a random-pitch MIDI effect into a drum rack/sampler holding your FX one-shots; on that FX track add an auto-pan whose LFO is sample-and-hold.
steps.expect: A different FX sample, at a different stereo position, each time.

steps.action: In clips, set per-note chance (probability) and a velocity range; map velocity to a synth parameter so dynamics also change timbre.
steps.expect: Note density and brightness vary from pass to pass.

steps.action: Inside the synth, run three independent sample-and-hold modulators on different parameters; for melodic voices use a repeating random (Turing-style) sequence on coarse pitch quantized to the minor scale, or a step sequencer with weighted note probabilities (root high, other notes medium/low).
steps.tool: Synth random modulators + quantizer + step sequencer
steps.expect: Melodic lines stay in key and centred on the root.

steps.action: Let the set run for a while, record it, then cut out the passages you like for a later track or reuse the designed sounds.
steps.expect: Raw material for an ambient piece.

verification: Every clip has a follow action and at least one track has a silence clip.
The random one-shot layer pans to a new position on each hit.
All melodic notes fall in the chosen scale and the root is the most frequent note.
